title: More ingredients, harder potion? What 38 recipes say

voiceover.text: A first-year cure for boils needs more ingredients than Polyjuice.
The Harry Potter Wiki lists seventy-two potions. Thirty-eight come with a recipe.
Together, they use ninety-six different ingredients.
Three in four of them appear in just one potion.
Even the most common, like valerian and wormwood, turn up in only four.
Valerian is the sleep herb, just like in real life.
So does a longer recipe make a harder potion?
Beginner potions use four ingredients on average. Advanced potions? Also four.
Cure for Boils, a beginner potion, needs eight. Wolfsbane Potion, an advanced one, needs just one.
The difficulty is in what goes in, and how you make it.
Polyjuice needs Boomslang skin, fluxweed picked at full moon, and lacewing flies stewed for twenty-one days.
And two potions share the exact same recipe: the Befuddlement Draught and the Confusing Concoction.
We counted every recipe on Querious, with one SQL query.
Group them your way, then download the result, or connect it to your own AI and tools.
Just remember: only thirty-eight potions have a recipe, and the ingredient groups are ours.
The data is open. The question is yours.
